note: Attacker controls the high bit of the second byte; when set, streaming mode is enabled, causing ctx->data to be heap-allocated and subject to realloc
In streaming mode ctx->data is heap-allocated with size 8192 (SPNG_READ_SIZE), making it eligible for realloc later
spng_decoded_image_size calls get_ancillary which triggers parsing of chunks before IDAT
get_ancillary calls read_chunks_before_idat to parse all chunks preceding the IDAT chunk
Local pointer 'data' is set to ctx->data before reading chunk bytes; this pointer becomes stale if ctx->data is reallocated
read_chunk_bytes calls read_data which reallocs ctx->data when chunk.length > ctx->data_size (8192) in streaming mode; the old buffer is freed, making 'data' a dangling pointer

code: void *buf = spng__realloc(ctx, ctx->data, bytes); ctx->data = buf;
note: realloc frees the old 8192-byte buffer and allocates a larger one; ctx->data now points to new memory, but local 'data' in read_chunks_before_idat still points to freed memory
Heap-use-after-free READ: memcpy reads chunk.length bytes from the stale 'data' pointer which points to freed heap memory, causing ASAN to report a use-after-free
